It lives here because register row 42 was a P0 for exactly one reason - there was no such place. B's banner would have announced 'Friday August 21 at 6:00 PM CDT' to all ten managers from a HARDCODED FALLBACK while fifteen files in this repo said 08-20, and nothing could adjudicate. Cory's ruling says the banner's date was right and the fifteen files were wrong. Any surface stating the deadline reads THIS key; a second hardcoded date anywhere is the defect recurring. Guarded against the nightly rebuild by test_config_local_rulings_survive.py - Sleeper has never heard of this key, so an unguarded rebuild would destroy it, which is exactly what happened to use_measured_ceiling on 08-17.
_opportunity_cap_why: 0.0 = LAYER OFF, Cory's ruling 2026-08-17 ('Remove 1'), after draft/audit/opportunity_adjustment_2026-08-16.md graded it for the first time: NEUTRAL on ordering in 17 of 18 cells, WORSE on level in 18 of 18 with every CI clear, and a SHUFFLED control (same magnitudes, randomly reassigned within position) performed identically — so it was carrying scale, not player information. It was also structurally one-sided: composite_z handles WR/TE/RB only, so QB/K/DEF carried exactly 0.0000 while RB/WR/TE reached +0.15, lifting three positions against three others in a VORP that compares across positions. Measured effect of turning it off on the live board: 51 of the top 60 overall ranks move and QB1 goes from rank 16 to 10. CENTRING it instead moved QB1 by ONE, because the distortion is the SPREAD (elite RB/WR/TE pinned at the cap while replacement sits near zero), not the level. HONEST LIMIT: the grade ran on reconstructed baselines that FLATTER the layer, so every positive number was an upper bound; its performance against Sleeper's own preseason baseline is unmeasurable until REC-2 grades it in January 2027. REVERSIBLE: restore 0.15 here, nothing else changes.
_player_volatility_in_tails_why: ON, ruled by A 2026-08-18 executing Cory's order ('fix!!!! floors and ceilings need to be corrected like I have agreed to' — his explicit override of the no-change-before-08-22 hold for THIS fix). Construction is VOLATILITY-WIRING-PREREG.md §2 verbatim: ceiling = mean x p90[cell] x f, floor = mean x p10[cell] / f, f = player's realized 2025 weekly cv over his cell median, normalized so the measured cell LEVEL is preserved (the §2 gate, tested in test_player_volatility_tails.py). Population fork ruled 2025-ONLY: persistence is measured on one-year transitions (rho +0.482/+0.605), so a 2024 cv on a 2026 board is outside the measured support; a player without a 2025 cv keeps his CELL constant (prereg §3's protection for the injury-return group: Evans, G. Wilson, Nabers, Daniels). Within-cell ceiling spread goes from exactly 1.0x to the measured 1.4-2.0x p10-p90 (ceiling_fix_blast_radius §2). Blast radius: bench branch + playerDollars only; ~~MEASURED_WEIGHTS.ceiling stays 0 and the composite ordering does not move — the weight question remains C1's, post-draft, per prereg §4 arm 3.~~ **STALE AS OF 09f94f99 AND CORRECTED BY THE RELAY 2026-08-18 (that correction said the live engine carried a ceiling weight of ~~0.45~~ — TRUE THEN, FALSE NOW).** ** SECOND CORRECTION 2026-08-21: Cory ruled the ceiling weight back to ZERO on 2026-08-20, so the original sentence's 'MEASURED_WEIGHTS.ceiling stays 0' is accurate again and the 08-18 correction is the stale one. This paragraph has now been wrong in both directions, which is why the rule is: read the constant at `engine.js:826`, never a description of it.** Cory ruled the weight and it SHIPPED; the sentence above describes the pre-ruling state. This is the FIFTH instance of register 5h — a weight ruling ships and the prose quoting the old number is never updated — and the first one found inside a CONFIG file, which is worse than a doc because a config reads as authoritative. **The blast radius of the ruling itself was measured at 0 of 12 seats (P74), so nothing Cory drafts moves; what was wrong was only this description.** Set to false to revert; nothing else changes.
_use_measured_ceiling_why: Cory 2026-08-17: 'We absolutely need to change draft board if we aren't considering upside.' He is right and the board could not express upside at all. proj_ceiling was mean + 1.036*proj_sd — and once REC-1 made proj_sd a per-BAND ratio, that is a monotone transform of the mean, IDENTICAL in shape for every player in a cell. Consequences, all three measured: the bench branch (which ranks on ceiling - mean) ranked Jordan Love, Baker Mayfield, Tyler Shough and Sam Darnold as the highest-upside players on the board, because a QB scores 350-400 and his spread is the largest absolute number almost by construction — engine.js's own comment says this 'measures SCALE, NOT UPSIDE' and added a hard cap to paper over it. CEILING_TIEBREAK, which is ON, was a NO-OP: breaking a near-tie by a monotone function of the mean just picks whoever was already ahead. And the composite ceiling weight was measured as collinear with value and zeroed — a true statement about the FORMULA, not a finding about upside. ON turns proj_ceiling into the MEASURED p90 of realized/projected outcomes (projection_error_calibration: 1,304 graded player-seasons, 20 cells). The same bench ranking then reads Gibbs, Bijan, McCaffrey, Jeremiyah Love, CeeDee Lamb. It also moves the board TOWARD anchors and away from deep fliers (band 33+ ceilings fall a median 7.5, bands 1-8 rise 17-30), which is the direction the barbell pass independently supports — that study read this same calibration directly and found anchors out-ceiling swings with zero overlap. This is a correctness fix on measured data, not a strategy bet. Set to false to revert; nothing else changes with it. Its sibling player_spread_in_sd stays OFF because those modifiers are hand-set constants the fit could not measure (permutation null [0.33, 5.65]).

draft._survives_rebuild: `preserve_local_rulings` in build.py keeps any key the committed file has and Sleeper does not supply, so the nightly rebuild cannot erase this. Guarded by test_config_local_rulings_survive.py::test_the_draft_start_ruling_survives_a_rebuild.
draft._why: Recorded as a RULING rather than left as a fallback. Before this, `src/dashboard.js` read `world.config.draft_time` and fell back to a hardcoded 6:00 PM with a <season>-08-22 date, and NO committed config set either — so the league was being shown a default nobody had confirmed. Cory confirmed the default is correct (CORY-ASKS A10). The keeper deadline went the same way on 08-18 and for the same reason: a hardcoded default doing load-bearing work is one unchecked sentence away from being wrong, and P71 is the case where fifteen internal files disagreed with a default and the DEFAULT was right.

pick_clock._what_it_voids: warroom_charts.js:76 — 'at eight seconds a pick nobody hovers, so it renders a [static form]' — is the clearest case: detail-on-demand was ruled out BY THE CLOCK, and it is the obvious answer to Cory's 'too busy and wordy'. Register 4e (the shortlist caption) was also declined partly on density-under-time. Both go back to B.
pick_clock._why: Recorded because it is a DESIGN PREMISE, not a scheduling detail. Fifty references across this repo argue from 'eight seconds a pick' — including live code comments in app.js, engine.js and warroom_charts.js, and the rationale for at least two shipped design decisions. None of them is functional logic (there is no timer), but several are the stated REASON a surface was kept sparse. With no clock those reasons are void and the decisions they justified have to be re-made on their merits.

draftable_scope._focus_vs_outer: focus (200) is the working scope: 150 drafted plus 50 of headroom for runs, injuries and reaches. outer (250) is the widest Cory named and is the right scope for a question that must not clip the tail. Neither is a tuned constant -- both are Cory's ruling, quoted above, and drafted is derived.
draftable_scope._why_not_all_700: The board carries 700 players because the ingest carries 700. Only 150 get drafted. Reporting anything -- coverage, accuracy, agreement -- over all 700 measures the deep bench nobody takes, and it makes real sources look broken: Draft Sharks covers 35% of 700 and 94% of the top 200. The first number is true and useless, the second is the one that decides a pick.
draftable_scope.cory_ruling_verbatim: We really just need to focus on top 200 players maybe 250
draftable_scope.drafted_derivation: teams * rounds = 10 * 15 = 150. Every player who will be on a roster when the draft ends. Cory's last pick is 148.
